steps.u: Add a 'scale servings' control to the recipe page: pick 2, 4, 6, 8 and the ingredient amounts update. We use SvelteKit.

steps.r:
{data.recipe.title}

    {#each data.recipe.ingredients as i}
  • {i.qty} {i.unit} {i.name}
    • {/each}

i.new_string:
{#each data.recipe.ingredients as i}
  • {scaleQty(i.qty, data.recipe.servings, servings)} {i.unit} {i.name}
    • {/each}

i.content:
it('rounds to quarters', () => { expect(scaleQty(1, 3, 4)).toBe(1.25) })
it('doubles', () => { expect(scaleQty(2, 4, 8)).toBe(4) })

steps.a: The control works and ingredient amounts update. Rounding to quarters means a 1 egg recipe scaled by 1.5 shows 1.5, fine, but small amounts like a pinch (0.1) round to 0. I noted that rather than special-casing it.

reference.summary: Added a servings selector (2, 4, 6, 8) to the SvelteKit recipe page that rescales ingredient quantities through a small helper, with unit tests. Quantities are rounded to quarters for readability, which rounds very small amounts to zero; that edge case was noted, not handled.
facts: ingredient amounts scale from the recipe's base servings

decisions.reason: quarters are easier to read in a kitchen than values like 0.333
